resolutions.researcher_notes: This is an auto-generated km-marker segment (UBTG-1 km0 to km56) of Saudi Aramco's Master Gas System (MGS) gas trunk corridor, not an independently named pipeline; no source names this exact 56-km/40-in segment. AGBI (independent) confirms the MGS 'came online in 1982' and is an existing operating network transporting gas east-to-west across Saudi Arabia; Pipeline Technology Journal (Al-Zahrani interview, independent) corroborates the Aramco-operated MGS gas trunk network. Status 'operating' is inferred at network level — the MGS has been operational since 1982 and this trunk segment carries gas within it. Cannot confirm operating status of the specific segment from any source; flag as network-level inference.

Fuel=Gas is well supported: both independent sources describe the Master Gas System, of which this UBTG trunk segment is a part, as a gas pipeline network carrying natural/associated gas east-to-west across Saudi Arabia (Al-Zahrani: 'transport gas from East to West Saudi Arabia'; AGBI: gas network, 12.5 bscf/d capacity). No ambiguity on the commodity.

LengthKnown=56 km is derived from the auto-generated km-marker route name (km0 to km56), i.e. from route geometry, not from any published source. No independent media, Aramco filing, or trade source states a 56-km length for this specific segment. Route-derived value; no media corroboration possible. UNRESOLVED.

Diameter=40 in has no source corroboration. It comes from the route/geometry dataset. Parallel MGS segments in the same corridor are logged at 48 in (UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56) and 56 in (Hawiyah-UBTG-1-km0); the Al-Zahrani/MGS-III material references 56-inch trunk pipelines, not 40-inch, so no source specifically supports 40 in for this line. UNRESOLVED.

Start/End country = Saudi Arabia. AGBI confirms the Master Gas System runs across the east-west corridor within Saudi Arabia (Ghawar field / Eastern Province to western provinces). This UBTG trunk segment sits inside that domestic corridor, so Saudi Arabia as both start and end country is supported at network level. No source gives the specific segment endpoints (UBTG km0 / km56 are internal route nodes), so only the country attribute is corroborated.

Owner1=Saudi Aramco 100%. Both independent sources attribute the Master Gas System to Saudi Aramco (Al-Zahrani: pipelines 'operated by Saudi ARAMCO'; AGBI: Aramco's master gas system). This UBTG segment is part of that Aramco-owned/operated MGS, so 100% Saudi Aramco ownership is supported at network level. No source addresses ownership of the individual segment, but the whole MGS is wholly Aramco-owned, so no conflict.
